items.name: THE COELACANTH
items.headline: Written off in the fossil record. Still swimming in the deep.
items.why_survives: Living populations persisted in deep marine habitats while the fossil record left a misleading gap.
items.where_now: African coelacanths still inhabit deep coastal waters of the western Indian Ocean.
items.note: This entry concerns Latimeria chalumnae. Rediscovery refers to scientific recognition in 1938, not a return from extinction. Survival does not imply that the species is safe from threats.
items.image_alt: Interpretive monochrome illustration of an African coelacanth in deep water

items.name: COBOL
items.headline: The language of yesterday still helps process the business of today.
items.why_survives: Established business logic and reliable decimal processing keep COBOL useful in critical systems.
items.where_now: Government and private-sector organizations still run financial and administrative applications in COBOL.
items.note: 1959 marks the CODASYL initiative; the first language version followed in 1960. No global transaction percentages are claimed. The illustration represents continuity, not current hardware requirements.
items.image_alt: Interpretive monochrome illustration of a computer terminal and mainframe cabinets

items.name: THE LAST BLOCKBUSTER
items.headline: Streaming took over. One video rental store kept the lights on.
items.why_survives: The store credits its survival to local support and visitors drawn to its unusual place in movie history.
items.where_now: Bend, Oregon: the remaining Blockbuster still offers physical movie rentals.
items.note: The claim concerns the remaining Blockbuster rental store, not every business using the name. Reuses GOODBYE artwork as an interpretive video-store scene; it is not a documentary image of the Bend premises.
items.image_alt: Interpretive monochrome illustration of a video rental store

items.name: LONDON GAS LAMPS
items.headline: Electric light took over. Some London streets still glow with gas.
items.why_survives: Heritage protection and specialist maintenance preserve surviving gas-powered street lights.
items.where_now: Working gas lamps remain in London, including protected examples in Covent Garden.
items.note: Preservation keeps these lamps alive; gas lighting is no longer the norm. This imagined streetscape is not a photograph of the protected Russell Street lamps.
items.image_alt: Interpretive monochrome illustration of a historic gas lamp in a London lane

items.name: THE WOLLEMI PINE
items.headline: A tree from an ancient lineage was hiding in an Australian gorge.
items.why_survives: An isolated wild population persisted; propagation now also keeps the species in botanic gardens.
items.where_now: Wild trees survive in Wollemi National Park, with cultivated trees in gardens worldwide.
items.note: Critically endangered. An ancient lineage does not mean an unchanged dinosaur-era species. The gorge is an imagined setting.
items.image_alt: Interpretive monochrome illustration of a Wollemi pine in a sandstone gorge

items.name: THE SOLENT HOVERCRAFT
items.headline: The future of transport became a daily crossing that never went away.
items.why_survives: Its ability to cross shallow water and land directly on shore suits the tidal beaches at Ryde.
items.where_now: Hovertravel still carries passengers between Southsea and Ryde on the Isle of Wight.
items.note: The passenger service survives, with newer craft. It is not the retired cross-Channel car service. Weather can interrupt crossings.
items.image_alt: Interpretive monochrome illustration of a modern passenger hovercraft crossing coastal water

items.name: MORSE CODE
items.headline: The telegram faded away. The dots and dashes stayed on the air.
items.why_survives: Amateur-radio practice, training and on-air communities keep radiotelegraphy in use.
items.where_now: ARRL's W1AW station provides Morse-code practice transmissions and bulletins.
items.note: Scope is international Morse code in amateur radio, not a claim that commercial telegram networks survive. Transmission schedules can change. Supporting explanation: https://www.arrl.org/cw-mode
items.image_alt: Monochrome straight Morse key connected to an amateur-radio transceiver beside headphones.

items.name: PNEUMATIC TUBES
items.headline: The capsule in the tube found a new job inside the hospital.
items.why_survives: Pneumatic systems move physical samples and medicines between wards and labs without manual courier trips.
items.where_now: Swisslog Healthcare offers pneumatic tube systems for hospital specimen transport.
items.note: Modern hospital systems are not surviving city-wide postal networks. Manufacturer evidence establishes an ongoing application, not adoption rates or universal clinical suitability. Packaging and route validation matter; no blanket safety claim is made.
items.image_alt: Interpretive monochrome illustration of a pneumatic transport capsule and receiving station

items.name: THE BRIENZ ROTHORN BAHN
items.headline: A decision to replace the steam railway was reversed. The mountain still hears its whistle.
items.why_survives: Local opposition saved the line; supporters and specialist maintenance help sustain seasonal steam operation.
items.where_now: Steam trains still climb from Brienz toward Rothorn Kulm in the Swiss Bernese Oberland.
items.note: Seasonal operation, with diesel substitution possible. Opened in 1892, suspended in 1914 and reopened in 1931; not uninterrupted service. The 1958 replacement decision was reversed. History: https://brienz-rothorn-bahn.ch/bahngeschichte/ Maintenance: https://brienz-rothorn-bahn.ch/lokomotiven/
items.image_alt: Interpretive monochrome illustration of a Swiss steam rack railway in an alpine landscape

items.name: VINYL RECORDS
items.headline: The record never stopped turning. It found another audience.
items.why_survives: A continuing market for physical records supports new pressings alongside digital listening.
items.where_now: RIAA reports continued US vinyl revenue growth in its 2025 recorded-music report.
items.note: The cited report covers the US market in 2025; revenue growth does not establish worldwide dominance or explain all buying motives.
items.image_alt: Interpretive monochrome illustration of a vinyl record being pressed in a modern record plant.

items.name: ZEPPELIN NT FLIGHTS
items.headline: The passenger airship returned—not as a liner, but as a view from the sky.
items.why_survives: A certified modern airship serves a niche market for seasonal sightseeing and special missions.
items.where_now: Deutsche Zeppelin-Reederei is selling 2026 sightseeing flights over Lake Constance and other German regions.
items.note: Verified 11 October 2026 against the operator’s active flight and booking pages. This is the modern semi-rigid Zeppelin NT, not uninterrupted survival of the historic rigid passenger liners. Flights are seasonal and weather-dependent.
items.image_alt: Interpretive monochrome illustration of a modern Zeppelin NT passenger airship over Lake Constance.

items.name: DOT-MATRIX PRINTERS
items.headline: The office went quiet. Somewhere, a print head is still rattling.
items.why_survives: Impact printing handles multipart forms; legacy-system compatibility keeps it useful for specialist work.
items.where_now: Epson currently sells wide-carriage impact printers for continuous and multipart forms.
items.note: Verified 12 October 2026 against Epson’s current US product listing, price and purchase controls. The survival explanation is an editorial inference from documented multipart-form, harsh-environment and legacy-system features; no worldwide sales-volume claim.
items.image_alt: Interpretive monochrome illustration of a modern dot-matrix printer feeding continuous multipart forms in a logistics workspace.

items.name: PHOTOGRAPHIC FILM
items.headline: The camera went digital. The darkroom did not disappear.
items.why_survives: An active analogue-photography market still has film, processing materials and learning resources.
items.where_now: ILFORD lists HP5 PLUS black-and-white film in 35mm, roll and sheet formats.
items.note: The checked product supports continued availability of black-and-white film, not every discontinued film stock. The market explanation is an editorial inference from the current product and processing ecosystem; no worldwide sales trend is asserted.

rating.note: Current manufacturer documentation supports ongoing 35mm, roll and sheet-film availability; original unbranded darkroom artwork passed all device layouts.

items.image_alt: Interpretive monochrome illustration of 35mm and medium-format film with developing equipment in a modern darkroom.

items.name: PS WAVERLEY
items.headline: The paddle wheels still turn beyond the museum quay.
items.why_survives: Preservation, volunteers and excursion demand keep the last seagoing paddle steamer in service.
items.where_now: Waverley’s operator lists final 2026 sailings for 17 and 18 October with tickets available.
items.note: Verified 14 October 2026 against the operator’s current sailing updates, timetable and booking pages. Service is seasonal and weather-dependent; the last-seagoing-paddle-steamer wording is the operator’s claim.

rating.note: Direct operator evidence includes dated October 2026 sailings and live booking instructions; original vessel artwork passed crop review.

items.image_alt: Interpretive monochrome illustration of a classic seagoing paddle steamer underway on a Scottish coastal firth.

items.name: SAN FRANCISCO CABLE CARS
items.headline: A moving cable beneath the street still pulls passengers up the hills.
items.why_survives: Public preservation and continuing transit and visitor demand keep the cable-powered system in service.
items.where_now: SFMTA lists the Powell–Mason and Powell–Hyde routes as active, with daily service and live arrival information.
items.note: Verified 15 October 2026 against SFMTA’s active route pages, current daily hours, schedules and live stop data. Street-running cable cars use a moving underground cable and are distinct from aerial gondolas, electric trolleybuses and historic streetcars. Temporary maintenance outages do not negate continued operation of the system.

rating.note: Current operator routes, hours and live stop data establish continuing service; original artwork passed responsive crop review. Catalogue fit is moderated because the system is intentionally preserved and globally famous.

items.image_alt: Interpretive monochrome illustration of a San Francisco street cable car climbing a steep hill above the moving cable slot.

items.name: BOOKMOBILES
items.headline: The library still arrives on four wheels.
items.why_survives: Mobile branches bring books, holds, internet access and programmes to communities beyond fixed library buildings.
items.where_now: Mobile Public Library’s 2026 schedule supports borrowing, holds and Wi-Fi aboard its bookmobile.
items.note: Verified 16 October 2026 against Mobile Public Library’s current service page and 2026 schedule. The operator documents borrowing, returns, hold pickup, outreach and Wi-Fi. This establishes an active local service in Mobile County, Alabama, not universal survival of every historic bookmobile programme.

rating.note: Current operator scheduling and service details establish active operation; the original artwork passed both responsive exports and device-layout review.

items.image_alt: Interpretive monochrome illustration of a contemporary bookmobile serving readers at a community stop.

items.name: PAGERS
items.headline: The little belt-worn receiver still carries urgent messages.
items.why_survives: Dedicated radio paging penetrates hospital structures and remains independent of Wi-Fi, cellular networks and mains power.
items.where_now: Spok currently supplies dedicated, encrypted and waiting-area pagers over its US healthcare paging network.
items.note: Verified 17 October 2026 against Spok’s current healthcare paging pages and active support documentation. The operator offers physical encrypted and conventional pagers, and documents live network and device support. This establishes continuing specialist healthcare use in the United States, not renewed mass-market consumer popularity or use by every hospital.

rating.note: Current operator and support pages establish active physical-pager service; the original hospital illustration passed responsive crop and device-layout review.

items.image_alt: Interpretive monochrome close-up of a physical alphanumeric pager clipped to medical scrubs in a modern hospital.

items.name: SWISS TELETEXT
items.headline: The blocky information pages still wait behind the television button.
items.why_survives: A fast, simple broadcast service still supplies news, sport, weather and accessible television subtitles.
items.where_now: SRF still directs viewers to Teletext, teletext.ch and subtitle page 777.
items.note: Verified 18 October 2026 against current SRF service and accessibility pages. The Swiss service remains available on television, web and app, with subtitle page 777. This does not claim every broadcaster retains Teletext or that the service is unchanged since 1984.

rating.note: Sources and scope rechecked 18 October 2026; original monochrome responsive artwork reviewed. Device-layout review remains a mandatory merge gate.

items.image_alt: Interpretive monochrome illustration of a television showing a blocky Teletext-style page beside a remote control.

items.name: THE KĀKĀPŌ
items.headline: The flightless night parrot survives through intensive conservation.
items.why_survives: Predator-free habitat, monitored breeding and conservation partnerships support a small, vulnerable population.
items.where_now: DOC reported 325 birds on 1 September 2026, with breeding populations on three protected New Zealand islands.
items.note: Rechecked 19 October 2026 against DOC’s current species page and dated 1 September 2026 release. The latter reports 325 birds after ninety chicks joined the tally; this remains a dated count, not a live census. The species remains critically endangered and depends on managed predator-free habitat. Breeding populations and fenced-sanctuary birds are not evidence of widespread recovery, and DOC states there is no public viewing site.

rating.note: Authoritative source and scope review completed 19 October 2026; original responsive artwork reviewed. Hosted device-layout review remains a merge gate.

sources.name: DOC — Kākāpō population reaches new milestone, 1 September 2026
sources.supports: Dated population milestone and continuing recovery programme.

items.image_alt: Interpretive monochrome natural-history illustration of a complete kākāpō on a protected native forest floor.

items.name: STUTTGART PATERNOSTERS
items.headline: The doorless lift cabins still make their endless loop through city hall.
items.why_survives: Stuttgart maintains its heritage lifts, including a modernised 1956 installation used during published weekday hours.
items.where_now: The city hall visitor page lists three paternosters and operating hours, subject to maintenance interruptions.
items.note: Rechecked 20 October 2026. Stuttgart’s current visitor page, dated 13 May 2026, lists three paternosters, weekday operating hours and possible maintenance closures. The Marktplatz-wing lift dates to 1956 and was modernised in 2004. A September 2026 municipal release also describes public paternoster rides. This confirms maintained operation at this site, not unchanged machinery or continuous availability. The illustration is a generic interpretive foyer, not an exact interior survey; it offers no advice on entering turning sections.

rating.note: Source, scope and responsive artwork review completed 20 October 2026. Hosted device renders and final visual review remain mandatory merge gates.

sources.name: City of Stuttgart — Open Day announcement, 15 September 2026
sources.supports: Recent municipal confirmation that paternoster rides remain part of city hall visits.

items.image_alt: Interpretive monochrome illustration of adjacent open wooden paternoster cabins passing a civic-office landing.

items.name: MAGNETIC DATA TAPE
items.headline: The cassette left the living room. Magnetic tape stayed in the data centre.
items.why_survives: High-capacity cartridges suit long-term archives and can be stored offline without continuous power.
items.where_now: Fujifilm currently offers modern LTO data tape for organisational backup and archiving.
items.note: Rechecked 21 October 2026. Fujifilm’s current LTO page presents tape for active archiving, backup and offline storage and describes a continuing multi-generation roadmap. This exhibit concerns modern digital LTO tape, not audio cassettes or VHS. Manufacturer evidence establishes an ongoing offering; no universal lifetime, cost-saving, capacity or ransomware-immunity claim is adopted. Offline storage still requires appropriate operational controls. Artwork is a generic interpretive data centre and tape library, not a particular product installation.

rating.note: Current manufacturer evidence, scope and responsive artwork reviewed 21 October 2026; hosted device-layout review remains a mandatory merge gate.

items.image_alt: Interpretive monochrome illustration of an LTO-style data cartridge before an automated tape-library bay.
